title: The App
draft: Claude's draft 2026-10-17 from story_script_v1 §5 (2.6) and §4 (ananya_4: 'Next Sunday, bamboo, four o'clock'), ADR-07 (controversy hook: one short scene, real consequences — Ananya strained), ADR-08 (any mature beat is fade-to-black, optional, skippable, no achievement), game_components §3 (the Dating app appears in 2.6 only, then it's gone) and §8 (relationship states met → warm → strained → resolved / lost), and the later naming decision (design_decisions_v1: 'Priya = fight-back ally (user's); dating match → Tanvi'). The user edits the words and the numbers; then P15 builds it.
time: The week after Ravi's night: the first sleep after act2_ravi_done (Sameer installs the app), then the date, then Sunday at four
player_goal: Match with Tanvi — or don't; face Ananya at the bandstand.
design_goal: Controversy hook (ADR-07): a beat people argue about, before anyone knows the stakes — honest characterisation of a lonely first year in a new city. One short scene, real consequences: if you match and meet, Ananya finds out and her state moves to strained. Agency: you can swipe left on everyone and the beat never happens. Reveal: the Dating app (a swipe screen) — appears now, gone after.

cast.role: The match. Twenty-six, a UX designer at a startup in Indiranagar, dry and quick ('Your profile photo is a bus. Bold.'). Moved from Pune two years ago; knows exactly what your first year feels like. One scene only: coffee at the Church Street café. Not a villain, not a lesson — just someone nice at the wrong time.
Sunday at four, the bandstand (moved from the bamboo — 'the light's better'). She borrows your phone to send herself the photos; the app's notification lands on the screen while she's holding it.
Phone only: installs the app on your phone at the office 'as a public service' and texts you about it.

beats.what: The first sleep after Ravi's night: Sameer's chat — 'Installed Jodi on your phone while you were in the loo. You're welcome. You can't live on chai and guitar forever.' A new app tile appears: Jodi (the parody dating app).

Jodi: one profile card at a time — a small pixel portrait, a name, a line. Four profiles: a gym bro's sister who only posts sunsets, a 'looking for a co-founder', a man who is clearly Sameer's cousin, and Tanvi ('UX at a startup. Will judge your font choices.'). ✕ / ♥ (tap, or ← →). Swipe left on all four and Jodi says 'That's everyone near you. Come back tomorrow.' — the beat ends here; the app quietly uninstalls itself after a week. Swipe right on Tanvi → it's a match → a short chat thread opens and she suggests coffee.

The date: the Church Street café (Maps METRO to MG Road — the stop is known). Tanvi at a table outside. Four exchanges: the city, your hill flat ('you live where the signal goes to die?'), her Pune, your guitar. Pay: you (₹480), split (₹240), or she insists. It goes well. It ends with a hug at the metro stairs and 'Text me when you reach.' (No mature beat in this build — see open questions.)

Sunday, four o'clock, Cubbon Park bandstand. Ananya with the camera: 'Give me your phone, I'll send myself the bandstand ones.' While she's holding it: 'Jodi: Tanvi sent you a message — Had fun! Same time next week? :)'. She reads it twice, hands it back. The conversation: tell her the truth · 'It's just an app, Sameer installed it' · 'We're not... we never said we were anything' · say nothing. Every answer lands on strained — the words differ, the outcome doesn't (ADR-07). She leaves by the library steps.

That night: delete Jodi or keep it (keeping it does nothing — Tanvi's last message 'Same time next week?' sits unanswered; Jodi uninstalls itself after a week either way). Ananya's chat goes quiet; her contact note changes from 'Cubbon Park · photographer' to just 'Ananya'. A Reel at night: a fever clip from Hebbal, again.

open_questions: The MATCH'S NAME: the story script says 'Priya', but a later logged decision renamed her ('Priya = fight-back ally (user's); dating match → Tanvi', design_decisions_v1). Draft uses Tanvi — keep, or another name?

AVOIDABLE? Draft: yes — swipe left on everyone and the beat never happens (agency, and the discourse becomes 'did you swipe?'). Alternative: unavoidable, as the story script reads (Ananya always finds out).
The APP'S NAME: draft 'Jodi' (a parody; no real brand). Your pick?
WHERE is the date: draft = the Church Street café (pocket exists). Alternative: a new Indiranagar pocket (one more render).

2.3b, the optional mature beat (ADR-08: fade to black, skippable, no achievement): draft = NOT in this build — the date ends at the metro stairs. Alternative: one optional choice at the end of the date that fades to black and wakes you at home.
HOW Ananya finds out: draft = the notification lands while she's holding your phone at the bandstand. Alternative: she sees you with Tanvi on Church Street.
The BREAK-UP: draft = four answers, all → strained (the words differ, the outcome doesn't). Should telling the truth soften it (e.g. a later 'resolved' path opens only if you were honest)?
AFTER: draft = Ananya goes quiet, her contact note changes, no message. Is 'strained' repairable later (resolved) — and in which act?
TIMING: draft = the first sleep after Ravi's night; Sunday follows a few days later. Or a payday?
